dates.notes: Signed in Beijing on 13 May 2025. Article 6(1) provides that the MOU enters into force on signature for three years and is automatically renewed for successive three-year periods unless one Party gives at least three months' written notice before the end of the term. Article 6(3) requires mutual agreement for termination. Article 7 states that the Chinese, Portuguese and English texts are equally authentic and that the English text prevails on divergence. The 'entered_into_force' date is the effective date of this non-binding interinstitutional arrangement, not a treaty ratification or deposit.

legal_nature.rationale: The Parties are China's National Development and Reform Commission and Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services, not the two States. The Brazilian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' official Concórdia guidance distinguishes an act in the name of the Brazilian State from an 'ato internacional interinstitucional', concluded by a ministry or public entity with its foreign counterpart; the latter is not concluded in the name of the Brazilian State and 'must always be non-binding and must not create international legal obligations for Brazil'. The MOU's Article 6 'entra em vigor' clause fixes the effective date of that administrative cooperation arrangement; it is not a treaty entry-into-force procedure. The text as a whole provides for no ratification, deposit or registration. The instrument is therefore a non-binding political/administrative act, not a treaty.

notes: Signed by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), an agency of the State Council of China.
Signed by the Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services (MDIC); the MDIC press release records signature by Executive Secretary Márcio Elias Rosa.

ai_provisions: Article 1 establishes a regular intergovernmental dialogue on AI and cooperation on AI infrastructure and high-quality datasets.
Article 1(2) provides for joint work on large language and multimodal models, technical exchanges and a joint AI laboratory.
Article 1(3) provides for cooperation on AI applications and platforms.
Article 1(4) provides for sharing practices on AI testing, evaluation, certification and regulatory policies, including security-detection tools and evaluation standards.
Article 1(5) provides for AI education and professional training.
Article 2 designates the NDRC and MDIC as lead entities and their departments as implementing bodies, with regular meetings.
relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding interinstitutional cooperation on AI development, applications, safety testing, regulation and education. No treaty obligation, ratification, depositary, enforcement, military-AI commitment or general AI regulation.
relevance.reason: A bilateral AI-specific memorandum of understanding between China's NDRC and Brazil's MDIC, signed on 13 May 2025. It creates a regular dialogue and cooperation across AI infrastructure, models, applications, safety testing, regulation and education. It is an interinstitutional act, not a treaty, and is not counted among binding instruments.

status_note: Non-binding interinstitutional MOU between China's NDRC and Brazil's MDIC. Article 6 provides that the MOU 'enters into force' on signature for three years and renews automatically; that is the effective date of the administrative cooperation arrangement, not treaty entry into force. The Brazilian MFA's Concórdia guidance classifies acts concluded by ministries or public entities with foreign counterparts as 'atos internacionais interinstitucionais', which are not concluded in the name of the Brazilian State and must always be non-binding; they must not create international legal obligations for Brazil. The text provides for no ratification, deposit, registration or treaty dispute settlement; disputes are settled by friendly consultations. It is therefore recorded as a non-binding political/administrative act, not a treaty.
